clue.text: Flash from aerial torpedo

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is the aerial service
a torpedo is called a fish in naval slang

explanation.surface: A gleam of light seen from a torpedo launched by an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' looks like a noun for a burst of light; here it is the adjective meaning showy and vulgar. Navy sailors called torpedoes 'fish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone showily, rakishly smart in a slightly disreputable way: a synonym.

clue.text: Is this your Irish address, padre?

definitions.text: Is this your Irish address, padre?

parts.words: Is this your Irish address, padre?
parts.note: the clue asks how an Irish speaker might respectfully address a priest, the honorific following 'your'

explanation.surface: Someone asks a priest whether this is where he lives in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a home location; it is a form of address. In Ireland a priest is traditionally called 'your Reverence'.
explanation.definitionFit: The honorific title used when speaking to a clergyman, as in the Irish 'your Reverence'.

clue.text: Opening for a final word

parts.note: amen is the word said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: An opportunity to say a last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A foramen is an anatomical hole, as in a bone: a technical synonym of opening.

clue.text: It is clean maybe, but has no spring

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the phrase could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A mattress is clean enough, but it has lost its bounce.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inelastic does not stretch and recover, so it lacks springiness: a descriptive equivalent.

clue.text: It's hell, controlling river-fish in the north

explanation.surface: Managing fish in northern rivers is a nightmare.
explanation.walkthrough: Heck is a mild substitute for 'hell' as an exclamation; in northern English dialect a heck is also a grating set in a river to trap fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A softened oath standing in for hell, and a dialect word for a fish-trapping grating in a stream.

clue.text: Cumberland food-merchant, so-called

explanation.surface: A trader in food from the county of Cumberland, as he is known.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke of Cumberland was nicknamed 'the Butcher' for his brutality after Culloden in 1746; 'so-called' signals that nickname. Cumberland is also a former English county, famous for its sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke's historical nickname, and a tradesman who sells meat: two separate senses.

clue.text: One of Jeremy's followers is an African crook

parts.note: bent means crooked or dishonest in British slang
a Hamite is a member of a group of North African peoples, in older terminology

explanation.surface: A disciple of some Jeremy turns out to be a dishonest African.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy is the philosopher Jeremy Bentham, founder of utilitarianism.
explanation.definitionFit: A Benthamite is a disciple of Bentham's utilitarian philosophy: a follower.

clue.text: Sampler from German city

explanation.surface: A taster from a town in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tries or tests something, and Trier, the ancient city on the Moselle in western Germany.

clue.text: Escaper who, they say, died in the Irish capital

indicators.note: they say means the word who is taken for how it is spoken

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like HOU
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

indicators.note: capital means the first letter, the capital letter, of the word Irish

explanation.surface: An escaped prisoner who reportedly met his end in Dublin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Irish capital' suggests Dublin; it is just I, the capital letter of 'Irish'. HOU is spoken like 'who'.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Houdini was the famous escapologist who freed himself from chains and locked tanks.

clue.text: Discharge gives scope for auditor

indicators.note: for an auditor, a listener, means the synonym of scope is taken as it is heard

parts.note: room means scope or latitude, as in room for manoeuvre

explanation.surface: An accountant is given leeway to sack someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' suggests an accountant; it means a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery mucous discharge from the eyes or nose: a synonym.

clue.text: Churchman has no ultimate right To his staff

indicators.note: having no ultimate letter means the final letter, here the R, is dropped from the church officer

parts.note: a verger is a church official who looks after the building

explanation.surface: A church official is denied the final say over his own employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees, but it is the rod of office a verger carries, named a verge.
explanation.definitionFit: A verge is a ceremonial rod carried before a dignitary, the very staff a verger bears: a synonym.

clue.text: Preserve against breakdown, if true

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: a breakdown has the letters of the following words collapsing into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone holding out against a nervous collapse, if the rumour is true.
explanation.definitionFit: A confiture is a fruit preserve such as jam: a synonym.

clue.text: Dances with suspect university types

parts.note: rum means odd or suspect in British slang
BAs are Bachelors of Arts, holders of a university degree

explanation.surface: Dancing alongside some dubious academics.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumbas are Cuban ballroom dances: plural examples of dances.

clue.text: Policy of reformers — it's set out in entrance

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters are placed inside the verb for enchant

parts.note: to entrance, stressed on the second syllable, is to charm

indicators.note: set out means the letters of the word before are laid out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A reforming party's programme is displayed in the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' looks like a doorway; it is the verb meaning to enchant. 'set out' rearranges ITS into TIS, which goes inside CHARM.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartism was the 1830s-40s British working-class movement for electoral reform built around the People's Charter.

clue.text: Composer takes pains with later arrangement

indicators.note: arrangement means the letters of the preceding words are put in a new order, as music is arranged

explanation.surface: A composer works hard at a subsequent arrangement of his music.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina was the great sixteenth-century Italian composer of sacred music.

clue.text: Number Ten backed by smaller group

indicators.note: backed means the word ten is written back to front

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister's residence supported by a lesser faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number Ten' suggests Downing Street, the British Prime Minister's home, but the words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine musicians, one fewer than ten: a group smaller than the ten just named.

clue.text: Notice to embassy to make concession

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a public notice
a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: A diplomatic message to an embassy in order to concede a point.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission is something granted or conceded in argument: a synonym.

clue.text: Subscription added to yours

parts.note: subscription here means what is written at the foot of a letter, which follows 'yours' in a common sign-off

explanation.surface: A further payment tacked on to what you already pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subscription' suggests a regular payment; it is the closing formula written under a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A word paired with 'Yours' to close a formal letter before the signature.

clue.text: 29 can't be this cipher

parts.note: the clue plays on the saying that anyone who is anybody is a person of note, so such a person cannot be a nobody

explanation.surface: A code that some person cannot crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 is ANYBODY; 'cipher' looks like a code, but means a person of no importance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher in the old sense of zero is a person of no importance, a nobody.

clue.text: Competent to give fine etc if ordered

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of the preceding words are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Able to impose a fine and so on, if instructed.
explanation.definitionFit: An efficient worker is capable and productive: a near synonym of competent.

clue.text: Original gardener's apron

parts.note: the original gardener is Adam in Eden, whose first covering was made of leaves of a fruit tree

explanation.surface: The work apron of a gardener from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Adam tended the Garden of Eden and, after the Fall, covered himself with fig leaves sewn together.
explanation.definitionFit: The leaf Adam wore for modesty, which became a byword for any covering of embarrassment.

clue.text: The core of any long fibre

indicators.note: the core of these words means the answer sits inside them, spanning the space

explanation.surface: The central strand of any lengthy thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fibre: a specific example of the general word.

clue.text: The battle is a farce under the French

indicators.note: under means in this down entry the farce sits below the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
a panto, pantomime, is a British Christmas stage farce

explanation.surface: A battle is a shambles under French command.
explanation.walkthrough: Lepanto (1571) was the sea battle where the Holy League defeated the Ottoman fleet. A panto is a British family Christmas show full of slapstick.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepanto names the famous naval battle off Greece in 1571.

clue.text: I agree freely about a race that shows the white feather

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters wrap round the race abbreviation
freely means the letters of I agree move about at will

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race

explanation.surface: Someone gladly concedes that a race showed cowardice.
explanation.walkthrough: Showing the white feather means cowardice, but here it is literal: 'freely' rearranges I AGREE into AIGREE, split round TT.
explanation.definitionFit: An aigrette is a white egret plume worn as an ornament: a literal white feather.

clue.text: This stripper has taken over little Teresa's turn

indicators.note: turn means the pet name is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: Tessa is a diminutive form of the name Teresa

explanation.surface: A stripper has taken over young Teresa's slot in the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripper' suggests a striptease act; an asset-stripper buys a company and sells off its parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes the compound for a corporate raider who buys firms to sell their valuable parts.

clue.text: They say Mrs Ruskin stood for Birkenhead initially

indicators.note: they say means the initials are taken for how they are spoken aloud

parts.note: F.E. Smith, Lord Birkenhead, was known by his initials F.E.

explanation.surface: Gossip has it that John Ruskin's wife stood as a candidate in Birkenhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Effie Gray married the critic John Ruskin; the marriage was annulled. The politician F.E. Smith became Lord Birkenhead, and his initials said aloud give the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphemia 'Effie' Gray was the wife of the Victorian art critic John Ruskin.

clue.text: Intensify study about note to Epistle

indicators.note: about means the study surrounds the note and the Epistle abbreviation

parts.note: a den is a private study
E is a musical note
Ep. is the abbreviation for Epistle

explanation.surface: Concentrate harder on study of a footnote to a biblical letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To deepen something is to make it stronger or more profound: a synonym.

clue.text: Dreamer has lost table-plan

indicators.note: has lost means the dreamer drops a word for a table from its letters

parts.note: an idealist is an impractical dreamer
a list is a table of items

explanation.surface: A daydreamer has mislaid the seating chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'table-plan' reads as a seating plan; it splits into 'table', removed, and 'plan', the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a scheme or intention, as in 'the idea is to leave early': a synonym of plan.

clue.text: Line taken in defence by Wagner?

explanation.surface: A defensive line held, perhaps by a German general.
explanation.walkthrough: The Siegfried Line was the German defensive fortification of both world wars; Siegfried is also an opera by Wagner.
explanation.definitionFit: The German Westwall fortifications bore this name, and so does the third opera of Wagner's Ring cycle.

clue.text: Anglo-Greek letters one follows with boredom

indicators.note: follows means the numeral for one comes after the two letter names

parts.note: en is the English name for the letter N
nu is the Greek letter N
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bored writer pens letters in English and Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness from lack of interest: a synonym of boredom borrowed from French.

clue.text: Cloth for tea spilt at riverside

indicators.note: at means the scrambled tea is placed next to the river, at its side

parts.note: the Taff is the river that flows through Cardiff in Wales

indicators.note: spilt means the letters of tea are scattered into another order

explanation.surface: A cloth for mopping up tea knocked over at a picnic by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilt' turns TEA into ETA, which goes at the side of the TAFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp woven silk fabric: an example of cloth.

clue.text: Unspecified member of a Gotham institution

parts.note: Gotham is a nickname for New York, abbreviated NY
a body is an organisation or institution

explanation.surface: Some nameless member of a New York institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Anybody means any person at all, an individual left unnamed: a synonym.
